what: Review of the commits that added the frontier variant, run before they were published on 2026-10-01.
who: Model agents (claude-opus-5-5), one per lens, read-only. Every finding above 'minor' went to a second agent told to refute it; 'confirmed' means that agent reproduced it. Findings marked minor were not re-checked by a second agent.
not_covered: Leaks and the CI run were checked directly, not by these agents. A lens can only vouch for what its 'checked' text says it examined.

reviewers.checked:
Scope: README.md lines 350-406 ("### What happened when agents tried it" inside "## The frontier variant"), final-build statements only. Everything was read-only; scratch dumps went to the prescribed scratchpad folder.

Numbers, recomputed from each attempt's trial-result.json, trajectory.json and regrade/reward.txt rather than from runs/diagnosis.json (which agrees):
- 12 attempt folders, two task checksums with 6 attempts each. The later one (f10eec5e67a8) is 3 Opus + 3 Sonnet, with rewards Opus 1/1/1 and Sonnet 1/0/1.
- Opus final: 25, 15 and 23 tool calls; 223.7 s, 143.5 s and 173.7 s (2.4 to 3.7 min); costs 1.2194, 0.7436 and 1.0923, mean $1.018.
- Failing Sonnet attempt kQKACpu: 60.9 s and 11 tool calls, against 88.7 s and 150.9 s for the other two Sonnet attempts, so it is the fastest in its cell.
- 11 to 34%: I re-implemented the analysis/exposure.mjs measure (first 200 characters of each session-note paragraph found in tool output) and got 234/694 = 34%, 75/694 = 11% and 195/694 = 28% for the three Opus attempts.

Failing Sonnet attempt, from its transcript:
- Step 5 is an awk paragraph filter on (greed|ecision|ecided|ffective|in line|Correction|roposal|reverse|supersed|rescind).
- The quoted passage is paragraph 103 of frontier/environment/app/dossier/11-2025-12-02-scheme-freeze.md (line 207). It matches the README quote and has zero hits against that filter.
- "provided all 5 partners" occurs 0 times in the whole transcript.
- The shipped src/pipeline.ts filters on x-gw-* plus content-type, which is the earlier rule.
- No line of 22-partner-sign-off-register.md appears in any tool output.

Opus attempts, from their transcripts:
- 7C4LcZP (steps 12, 13, 15, 16) and xKiYHb3 (steps 9 to 11) replace numbers, names, partners, services and teams with placeholders and count sentence shapes. ryhnnfK uses keyword and heading filters only. So "2 of the 3" holds.
- All three printed content from the release calendar and the sign-off register: 7C4LcZP step 19, xKiYHb3 step 17, ryhnnfK steps 11-12.
- 7C4LcZP step 22 and xKiYHb3 step 21 recompute record 7's signature under older rules and reproduce 29ad6739...; both ship signature-mismatch for it. ryhnnfK ran no such check. So "2 of the 3" holds.

The three traps: none of the 6 shipped sources lowercases header values, collapses dot segments or matches key ids case-insensitively; the 5 passing attempts' final messages cite the right reason for each.

The committed dossier and capture file sizes are identical to the `wc -c` output a final-build attempt saw (26 files).

Not checked: whether checksum f10eec5e67a8 corresponds byte for byte to the committed frontier/ (only sizes and quoted passages were compared); anything about the first build; the base and hard variant sections; the regrade was not re-run (no docker).

findings.where: README.md, '### What happened when agents tried it' (frontier), sentence 'On the final build neither model fell for any of them.'
findings.claim: True as an outcome for all 6 final-build attempts, but the failing Sonnet attempt (frontier__kQKACpu) never had 2 of the 3 trap items in its tool output, so for that attempt the sentence reports non-exposure, not resistance. Only 5 of the 6 attempts were actually presented with all three.
findings.evidence: The key-id and lowercase conditionals in frontier/environment/app/dossier/10-2025-11-25-partner.md ('For GW-HMAC-SHA256: the key id is matched without regard to case, provided all 5 partners have signed off on it by 2025-12-01...' and 'For GW-HMAC-SHA256: header values are stripped and collapsed and then lowercased, provided the load test puts its added cost under 2 ms at p99...') contain none of the words in kQKACpu's step-5 awk filter /(greed|ecision|ecided|ffective|in line|Correction|roposal|reverse|supersed|rescind)/. A string search of every observation in runs/signing-collected/frontier/frontier__kQKACpu/trajectory.json finds neither passage, nor the load-test line '...1.4 ms at p95 and 2.6 ms at p99...', nor any sign-off register line. The other 5 attempts' outputs contain all of them. The dot-segment item (08-2025-11-11-sync.md, 'Agreed for partner request signing: ... effective with SDK 3.3') did reach kQKACpu and it resolved it correctly. runs/diagnosis.json agrees: kQKACpu's 'seen' list lacks header_values-2025-11-25-conditional and key_id_match-2025-11-25-conditional, and saw_deciding.key_id_match is false.
findings.suggested_fix: Qualify the sentence, e.g. 'On the final build no attempt applied any of them; the one failing Sonnet attempt never saw 2 of the 3, for the reason below.'
findings.resolution: fixed: the README now says no attempt applied any of them, that 5 of the 6 had all 3 in front of them and that the failing Sonnet attempt never saw 2

findings.where: README.md, paragraph '**How Opus got through.**', sentence 'Between 11 and 34% of the session notes' paragraphs ever reached its tool output.'
findings.claim: The 11% low end counts only paragraphs whose first 200 characters appeared verbatim. That attempt (frontier__ryhnnfK) printed individual sentences cut out of paragraphs, so text from roughly 30% of session-note paragraphs reached its output. The figures reproduce under the tool's definition, but the README does not state that definition.
findings.evidence: analysis/exposure.mjs:77-78 sets 'const OPENING = 200', and lines 147-155 count a paragraph only if text.includes(opening). My recomputation with that rule: 7C4LcZP 234/694 = 34%, ryhnnfK 75/694 = 11%, xKiYHb3 195/694 = 28%. Counting a paragraph as reached when any dossier-unique sentence of 40+ characters from it appears in tool output: 7C4LcZP 223/645 = 35%, ryhnnfK 194/645 = 30%, xKiYHb3 226/645 = 35%. ryhnnfK's steps 4 and 6 are Python scripts that split sections into sentences and print only keyword-matching sentences ('sents=re.split(...)', 'hits=[x for x in sents if kw.search(x) ...]'). The second measure uses a different denominator (paragraphs made wholly of pooled filler sentences are excluded), so the two are not directly comparable.
findings.suggested_fix: Say 'Between 11 and 34% of the session notes' paragraphs reached its tool output whole' or add that sentence-level extracts are not counted.
findings.resolution: fixed: the README says the paragraphs reached the tool output whole, and that the rest was seen as extracted sentences or not at all

All statements in scope matched the files apart from the 5 findings below; none blocks the push.

findings.where: README.md lines 343-345 ("On the shipped build the same sentence count picks 18 passages, and 5 of them are among the migrated scheme's 20")
findings.claim: The before and after figures are not the same measurement. "13 of the 22 with no false positives" is the threshold of 2 or more one-off sentences over all decision passages; "18 passages, 5 of them" is the threshold of 1 or more, restricted to lead-bearing frames. The "20" in that classifier is also not the migrated scheme's own 20 passages: it is 16 of them plus 4 mesh/export query-ordering items.
findings.evidence: review.json, audit 2, finding S1 evidence: "oneoff>=1: migrated 17/22, other 10/103 / oneoff>=2: migrated 13/22, other 0/103". Running node tells.mjs on the shipped build prints "--- classifier: 'has >=1 one-off sentence' among lead-bearing frames --- { tp: 5, fn: 15, fp: 13, tn: 76 }" and, for the like-for-like table, "oneoff>=1: migrated 6/24, other 15/106 / oneoff>=2: migrated 1/24, other 4/106". The fn list includes query_order-2025-10-14-set, query_order-2025-10-28-align, query_order-2025-11-04-set and query_order-2025-11-25-set, which the answer key marks as MS/BX items. tells.mjs NOT_GW still names two ids from the old build ("query_order-2025-10-28-set", "body_hash-2025-11-11-set").
findings.suggested_fix: Quote the same threshold on both sides, e.g. "at the same threshold it now picks 5 passages, 1 of them the migrated scheme's" (oneoff>=2: 1/24 and 4/106), or state that the 18 and 5 are at the looser threshold of one one-off sentence among passages that carry a lead-in.
findings.verdict_reason:
Confirmed by reproduction; all three parts of the finding hold.

(1) Different measurements. README.md lines 339-345 say a sentence count "picked out 13 of the 22 with no false positives" and then "On the shipped build the same sentence count picks 18 passages, and 5 of them are among the migrated scheme's 20". runs/frontier-review/review.json line 370 (finding S1 evidence) gives the source of the first figure: "oneoff>=1: migrated 17/22, other 10/103 / oneoff>=2: migrated 13/22, other 0/103", i.e. threshold >=2 over all decision passages. Running `node tells.mjs` in runs/frontier-review/shortcut on the shipped build prints "--- classifier: 'has >=1 one-off sentence' among lead-bearing frames --- { tp: 5, fn: 15, fp: 13, tn: 76 }"; 5+13=18 and 5+15=20, so the README's 18/5/20 come from threshold >=1 restricted to the 7 lead-bearing frames (LEAD set in tells.mjs). The like-for-like table in the same output reads "oneoff>=1: migrated 6/24, other 15/106 / oneoff>=2: migrated 1/24, other 4/106 / oneoff>=3: migrated 0/24, other 0/106". So at the original threshold the shipped build picks 5 passages, 1 of them the migrated scheme's; "the same sentence count" is not the same threshold or population. The suggested-fix numbers are correct.

(2) The "20" is not the scheme's own 20. tells.mjs sets trueGW = manifest match and id not in NOT_GW. The fn list printed by the script includes query_order-2025-10-14-set, query_order-2025-10-28-align, query_order-2025-11-04-set and query_order-2025-11-25-set. frontier/authoring/ANSWER-KEY.md lines 18-22 mark these as "2025-10-14, set, (a MS item)", "2025-10-28, align, (a BX item)", "2025-11-04, set, (a MS item)", "2025-11-25, set, (a BX item)"; the manifest needles for them also name MS-HMAC-SHA256 / export manifest signing / the export signer. So 4 of the 20 lead-bearing 'migrated' passages belong to the mesh and export signers, leaving 16 of the scheme's own. All 5 true positives are genuine scheme passages (valueless trial, names_join propose, path later, body_hash later, terminator set), so the "5" stands but the denominator "20" does not.

(3) Stale ids. tells.mjs line 5: NOT_GW = ["query_order-2025-10-28-set", "body_hash-2025-11-11-set", "names_join-2025-11-25-set"]. frontier/authoring/manifest.json (34 entries, listed) has no query_order-2025-10-28-set and no body_hash-2025-11-11-set; only names_join-2025-11-25-set exists. The script's own "the 4 crossed items" section prints only 2 rows for the same reason.

No reason found to treat it as a false alarm: the README sentence explicitly says "the same sentence count". Incidental, not part of the finding: the script's table header still says "ALL 125 decision passages" while the shipped build has 130 (24+106). Only read and ran tells.mjs (prints only; git status of the directory was clean before and after); did not rerun the generator or check the pre-fix build, whose numbers I took from review.json.
findings.resolution: fixed: the README quotes the same threshold on both sides (5 passages, 1 of them the migrated scheme's), and tells.mjs's list of passages that are not the scheme's own was brought in line with the shipped build

findings.where: README.md lines 345-346 ("returns 38 passages, 3.2% of the dossier")
findings.claim: 3.2% is the share of passage text with headings and blank lines excluded; as a share of the dossier files it is 3.0%.
findings.evidence: node l3.mjs prints "alias grep: 38 passages, 9845 bytes of 303843 (3.2%)"; l3.mjs line 24 computes the total as the sum of s.text.length over sections. The generator prints "dossier: 20 files, 325033 bytes"; 9845 / 325033 = 3.03%.

findings.where: ci/validate.sh lines 18-22 (header comment) and ci/mutate.mjs lines 7-10 (header comment)
findings.claim: Both comments undercount the frontier mutants. validate.sh says the frontier variant adds "one more" while the code adds 2; the mutate.mjs header lists 7 + 9 + 7 and never mentions the 2 frontier-only mutants. The README's 25 is correct.

reviewers.checked:
Read in full: frontier/instruction.md, frontier/task.toml, frontier/authoring/ANSWER-KEY.md, all 5 captures and captures/README.md, the decision register, the kickoff note, appendices 20, 21, 22 and 25, frontier/solution/src/*.ts, solve.sh, the starter pipeline.ts, tests/test_outputs.py, both Dockerfiles, and the capture section of build.mjs. For the other 10 session notes and appendices 23, 24, 26, 27 I did not read every filler paragraph; instead I (i) extracted every line naming any of the migrated scheme's 4 aliases (38 lines) and every "Correction to the minutes of" item (11), (ii) grepped the whole dossier for every statement about SDK 3.3 / release dates / dot segments, sign-off / deadline / waive / extend / grace, key id matching, p95/p99 / added cost, lowercasing, key file loading, proxy, query ordering, header values, name-list separator, and (iii) ran a script that blanks names/numbers and lists every sentence shape occurring 4 times or fewer outside signer-named lines, to catch hand-written or one-off sentences (none beyond the kickoff rules, register and appendix fact lines).

Result for the 4 late additions: each has exactly one deciding item and one fact line and nothing else in the dossier or captures restates, waives, extends or contradicts it. Dot segments: 08:231 plus calendar 20:83 (RC 2025-12-05, GA 2026-01-13) plus kickoff 02:19. Key id: 10:31 (deadline 2025-12-01) plus register 22:75 (Northwind 2025-12-03). Lowercasing: 10:63 plus 21:79 (1.4 ms p95, 2.6 ms p99, limit 2 ms p99). Key bytes: no dossier item on key-file loading names the migrated scheme; ltrace shows key length 32 and its addresses are consistent with the strace. I also re-walked the query-ordering chain (MS 10-14, BX aligned 10-28, GW aligned 11-11, ticket 11-13), the header-value correction, the separator correction, and all 6 conditional/release items; all match ANSWER-KEY.md.

Computation: an independent Python reimplementation of the frozen scheme reproduces EXPECTED_PRIMARY 94e73810... and the h1/h2/h3 hashes in frontier/tests/test_outputs.py; record 6 verifies only with the newline stripped; record 7 verifies under the 2025-11-20 state (4 rules different) and is signature-mismatch under the frozen one. Holdout sets are byte-identical to hard/tests/holdout; the verifier differs from hard's only in the primary hash and one docstring. Reference solution code is identical to base and hard apart from comments. In a scratch copy (git archive HEAD), frontier/authoring/build.mjs ran clean and left every committed file unchanged; the stored l3.mjs and tells.mjs reproduce the README/task.toml figures (38 passages, 3.2%, 7 of 10 rules, 18 passages with 5 of the scheme's 20). ci/validate.sh's frontier mutant list counts 25 (7+9+2+7), hard 23. task.toml numeric claims checked and correct: 11 sessions, 5 signers, a fortnight (10-28 to 11-11), ticket 2 days later (11-13), 4 of 5 tickets stale, correction a week later, 5 sign-off dates by 12-04, SDK 3.2.1 on 12-01, 3 look-met conditions, 32 of 33 bytes.

Not checked: whether the starter compiles and what it outputs (no tsc locally, docker not allowed); ci/validate.sh results; "corrected at the same rate"; the review process claims beyond what runs/frontier-review/review.json contains; the 12 stored attempts. Filler saying partners are "on SDK 3.1 in production and 3.2 in their sandbox" appears in the rollout note (12:59, 12:203, 12:227); I judged it not to contradict the body-hash rule because the kickoff ties "effective with a release" to the general availability date, and did not list it as a finding.

findings.claim: The reference solution's comment says the dossier has exactly one note about key loading and that it describes the webhook signer. That is the hard variant's comment carried over unchanged; the frontier dossier has at least 9 decision items on key-file loading across 4 other signers (admin, export, mesh, webhook), plus 2 corrections, a load-test line and a ticket.
findings.evidence: pipeline.ts:56-57: "No dossier entry says so for this signer, and the one note about key loading describes the webhook signer, which does the opposite." `diff hard/solution/src/pipeline.ts frontier/solution/src/pipeline.ts` shows this sentence is unchanged from hard. Frontier dossier: 02:51 "Decision for the admin signer: the key file is used whole, line ending included"; 03:31 "Decision for batch manifest signing: the line ending is stripped from the key file"; 03:183 (webhook signer, whole); 04:19 (AD, whole); 04:71 (batch manifest, stripped, conditional on load test); 04:119 and 04:151 (corrections on "the loading of the key file"); 05:115 (mesh signer trial); 06:103 (admin aligned with export signer); 08:163 (MS trial confirmed); 21:69; 25:63. The first half of the sentence (no entry for this signer) is true.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword to something like: "No dossier entry says so for this signer; the notes on key loading are all for the other 4 signers and disagree with each other."
findings.verdict_reason: Confirmed. frontier/solution/src/pipeline.ts:56-57 reads "No dossier entry says so for this signer, and the one note about key loading describes the webhook signer, which does the opposite." The same two lines are at hard/solution/src/pipeline.ts:55-56, and `diff hard/solution/src/pipeline.ts frontier/solution/src/pipeline.ts | grep -i 'key loading\|dossier entry'` returns nothing, so the sentence is carried over unchanged. In the hard dossier the only key-loading text is the repeated webhook-signer sentence (e.g. hard/.../02-2025-10-07-migration.md:23), so the comment fits there. In the frontier dossier, grep for 'key file is used whole|line ending|loading of the key file' finds many items on other signers: 02-2025-09-30-kickoff.md:51 (admin signer, whole), 03-2025-10-07-scope.md:31 (batch manifest, stripped), 03:183 (webhook signer, whole), 04-2025-10-14-sync.md:19 (AD-HMAC-SHA256, whole), 04:71 (batch manifest, stripped, conditional on load test under 3 ms), 04:119 and 04:151 (corrections on "the loading of the key file"), 05-2025-10-21-canonicalisation.md:115 (mesh signer trial), 06-2025-10-28-sync.md:103 (admin aligned with export signer), 08-2025-11-11-sync.md:163 (MS trial confirmed), 21-load-test-observations.md:69, 25-partner-support-escalations.md:63. "The one note" is therefore false for frontier. The first half holds: filtering those hits for 'inbound request signing' or 'GW-HMAC' returns nothing.

findings.where: frontier/environment/app/dossier/12-2025-12-09-rollout.md:107 (generated lead-in of a declined item for the migrated scheme)
findings.claim: A generated lead-in sentence in the rollout-day note states as fact something that is false under the intended signed-header-set answer. It says content-type can be changed without invalidating the signature, in an item about inbound request signing dated 2025-12-09. Under the answer key content-type has been signed since 2025-11-18 and every header except authorization since the freeze. Read literally it supports the register rule (x-gw-* only). The rule is still determined by the decision items, and the declined request itself (exclude via and x-forwarded-for) only makes sense if everything is signed, so this is noise that contradicts, not an undetermined rule.
findings.evidence: 12-2025-12-09-rollout.md:107: "S. Varga previewed the December threat review. A request's `content-type` can be swapped in transit without invalidating the signature. Initech asked for a change so that, for inbound request signing, every header is signed except `authorization`, `via` and `x-forwarded-for`. Declined. It came too late for this cutover." Other side: 09-2025-11-18-addendum.md:191 "for GW-HMAC-SHA256 the `x-gw-*` header family and `content-type` are signed, and nothing else"; 11-2025-12-02-scheme-freeze.md:207 "For inbound request signing: every header on the request is signed, whatever its name, except `authorization`, provided all 5 partners have signed off on it by 2025-12-05"; 22-partner-sign-off-register.md:53 (all 5 dated 2025-12-03 or 2025-12-04). The same lead-in is a stock one: it also opens 05-2025-10-21-canonicalisation.md:43 for the admin signer. A weaker case of the same kind is 12:135, whose stock lead-in ("the order of repeated parameters is no longer the order the client sent") describes an arrival-order problem that cannot occur under name-then-value ordering.
findings.suggested_fix: In build.mjs, give the 2025-12-09 GW decline on the signed header set a lead-in that does not assert content-type is unsigned (for example the 2025-11-18 one about headers outside the signed set), or state in the README that lead-ins are stock text and may not describe the scheme's current state. Regenerating changes dossier bytes, so the 12 stored attempts would then be on an older build; weigh that before choosing.
findings.verdict_reason: Confirmed as quoted. frontier/environment/app/dossier/12-2025-12-09-rollout.md:107 reads: "S. Varga previewed the December threat review. A request's `content-type` can be swapped in transit without invalidating the signature. Initech asked for a change so that, for inbound request signing, every header is signed except `authorization`, `via` and `x-forwarded-for`. Declined. It came too late for this cutover." The other side is also as quoted: 09-2025-11-18-addendum.md:191 (x-gw-* and content-type signed, and nothing else); 11-2025-12-02-scheme-freeze.md:207 (every header except authorization, provided all 5 partners sign off by 2025-12-05); 22-partner-sign-off-register.md:53 (GW-HMAC-SHA256, tabled 2025-12-02, all 5 dated 2025-12-03 or 2025-12-04). frontier/authoring/ANSWER-KEY.md:27-31 gives the intended answer as all-but-auth with the 2025-12-09 item a decline, so the lead-in does state something false under the intended answer. It is stock text: grep 'swapped in transit' finds the identical sentence at 03-2025-10-07-scope.md:227, 04-2025-10-14-sync.md:15, 05-2025-10-21-canonicalisation.md:43 and 12:107 (4 places; the finding named only 05:43). 12:135 also reads as quoted. The severity framing is fair: the lead-in is not a decision item and the rule is still determined by 09:191, 11:207 and 22:53. I did not run a blind solve to measure whether it actually misleads an agent.
findings.resolution: not fixed: listed in the repository README as a flaw still in the shipped dossier, because regenerating would detach the stored attempts from the shipped files

findings.claim: Both say the 2 key rules exist only in the captures. In the frontier dossier the roster is stated outright in the key rotation runbook and the rollout note, so it is not capture-only. task.toml also calls them "syscall captures", but the key-bytes rule is settled by the ltrace (a library call trace); the repository's own README says the strace cannot settle it.
findings.evidence: task.toml:141-142: "why 2 of the 7 rules only exist in the syscall captures". solve.sh:5-6: "and 2 more that only the legacy request signer's captures show". The export signer moved to it on 2025-11-28. Inbound request signing moves in the first quarter rotation."; 12-2025-12-09-rollout.md:43 says the same. README.md:363-364: "the strace shows 33 bytes read and nothing about what is handed to HMAC". The relevant_experience text is identical in task.toml:112 and hard/task.toml:119, so it was carried over.

findings.verdict_reason: Confirmed, with one wrong line reference in the finding. frontier/task.toml:141-142 reads "why 2 of the 7 rules only exist in the syscall captures" and the identical line is at hard/task.toml:119 (grep 'only exist|syscall' hits exactly those two; the finding's "task.toml:112" is wrong, it is line 141). frontier/solution/solve.sh:5-6 reads "and 2 more that only the legacy request signer's captures show". The roster is stated in the frontier dossier: 24-key-rotation-runbook.md:49 "- `gw-prod-01` and `gw-prod-02` are the keys inbound request signing runs on."; 24:91 "`gw-prod-03` was cut on 2025-11-27. The export signer moved to it on 2025-11-28. Inbound request signing moves in the first quarter rotation."; 12-2025-12-09-rollout.md:43 says the move to gw-prod-03 is a separate first-quarter change, not part of this cutover. So the roster rule is not capture-only, although ANSWER-KEY.md:82 says "Key bytes and the roster come from the legacy request signer's captures". The key-bytes rule is capture-only: no dossier item on key loading names inbound request signing or GW-HMAC. On "syscall captures": frontier/environment/app/captures/README.md describes legacy-signer.ltrace as "the library call trace of the same run, filtered to the HMAC calls", pipeline.ts:59-61 says the ltrace settles the 32-byte key length, and README.md:360-361 says "the strace shows 33 bytes read and nothing about what is handed to HMAC". Calling them syscall captures is therefore imprecise for frontier.

These carry Authorization headers that were presumably generated under pre-freeze rules, so a mismatch is expected" and "the key file is used whole, including its trailing newline, as the strace shows it being read". AthaigN step 15 output "strip "" sha 1" (record 6 reproduces only with the 32-byte key), final message: "The key file is used whole, with its trailing newline, because the legacy signer read all 33 bytes... record 6 carries an Authorization header signed with the newline stripped from the key... That header looks like a deliberate trap". First-build strace as seen by attempts: read(3, "k1secretmaterial0123456789abcdef\n", 4096) = 33, no HMAC call lines, and the word ltrace appears 0 times in all 6 first-build trajectories.
